mainTopic: Chullin 131b: the poor-gifts and the owner's rights, whether לוים must give the priestly gifts, and whether a כהנת may receive them
overview: The גמרא first finishes a ברייתא about the gifts for the poor. It brings the פסוקים for the gifts of a grain field (לקט, שכחה, פאה) and of a tree (שכחה, פאה). The owner has no טובת הנאה in these gifts, meaning he cannot choose who gets them, because the תורה says to 'leave' them. מעשר עני is different: the תורה says to 'give' it, so the owner may choose. Even a poor owner must give these gifts, and בית דין takes them from him if he does not. The גמרא then asks whether לוים count as 'the people' who must give the זרוע, לחיים and קבה to a כהן, which רב was unsure about. Several ברייתות are brought and pushed off, until one seems to refute רב outright. רב answers that this is a מחלוקת of תנאים, and he is unsure which one to follow. מרימר rules like רב and like רב חסדא. Finally, רבא challenges עולא for giving the gifts to a כהנת, and עולא's reply continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Verses for the three gifts of standing grain
steps.stepSummary: Finishing the list of three gifts from standing grain (שכחה and פאה, along with לקט) and bringing their sources from the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...and the forgotten sheaves and the corner of the field. As it says: 'When you reap the harvest of your land, do not finish the corner of your field... and the gleanings of your harvest...' and: 'When you reap your harvest in your field and forget a sheaf in the field.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list of three gifts from a grain field (לקט, שכחה, פאה) and shows which פסוקים they come from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק (ויקרא) is the source for פאה and לקט. The second פסוק (דברים) is the source for שכחה, a sheaf that the owner forgot in the field. So all three grain gifts have a clear source in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Forgotten produce, such as a sheaf left behind by mistake, which goes to the poor
The corner of the field, left unharvested for the poor
Gleanings, the stalks that fall during harvesting, which go to the poor
A sheaf of grain

phrases.english: and the forgotten sheaves, and the pe'a,
as it is written: 'And when you reap the harvest of your land,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:22

phrases.english: you shall not wholly reap the corner of your field when you reap
and the gleaning of your harvest, etc.'
'When you reap your harvest in your field
phrases.notes: דברים 24:19

phrases.english: and have forgotten a sheaf in the field.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list of poor-gifts, which began before this section.
steps.raayaObject: The ברייתא's claim that standing grain carries three poor-gifts: לקט, שכחה and פאה
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 23:22 for פאה and לקט; דברים 24:19 for שכחה

steps.title: Two gifts from a tree: forgotten fruit and the corner
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says a tree carries two poor-gifts, שכחה and פאה. Both are learned from one פסוק about olive trees, as read by the school of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two gifts come from a tree: forgotten fruit and the corner. As it says: 'When you beat your olive tree, do not go over the boughs after you.' The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: do not take all its glory from it. 'After you' refers to forgotten fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to trees and shows that one פסוק teaches two gifts: פאה and שכחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תפאר sounds like תפארת, 'glory.' So 'do not תפאר' means do not strip the tree of all its fruit, which is פאה. The word 'after you' means fruit left behind you, which is שכחה. לקט is not listed for trees, because the פסוק does not teach it there.

keyTerms.meaning: A tree
Going over the boughs; read as related to תִּפְאֶרֶת, 'glory'
Its glory or splendor, meaning the tree's full crop of fruit
Beat or knock down, as when harvesting olives

phrases.english: Two that are from a tree:
the forgotten fruit and the pe'a,
as it is written: 'When you beat your olive tree
phrases.notes: דברים 24:20

phrases.english: you shall not go over the boughs after you,'
and the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
that you should not take its splendor from it,
phrases.notes: תפאר sounds like תפארת, 'splendor.' Don't take every last bit of fruit; that leftover is the פאה.

phrases.english: 'After you': this is forgotten fruit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the gifts of a grain field to the gifts of a tree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tree carries two poor-gifts, שכחה and פאה, both learned from דברים 24:20.

steps.title: Why the owner cannot choose who gets the gifts
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the owner has no טובת הנאה in any of these gifts, and the גמרא asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in all of them, the owners have no right to choose who receives them. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the rule that the owner cannot pick which poor person gets these gifts, then asks why. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טובת הנאה is the small benefit an owner gets from choosing who receives a gift, for example giving it to a poor relative or friend. The ברייתא says the owner does not have even this. The גמרא wants the source for that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner's 'benefit of discretion': the right to choose who gets the gift
Owners, here the owner of the field or tree
And all of them, meaning every poor-gift in the list

steps.confusionAlert: טובת הנאה does not mean the owner may eat the gifts himself. That is obviously forbidden. It means he cannot even decide which poor person receives them.

phrases.english: And all of them, there is not in them
the benefit of discretion for the owners,
phrases.notes: He means the owner can't hand the gifts to a poor person he prefers. Whichever poor person takes them first owns them.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the sources of each gift to a rule that covers all the gifts together.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or reason that the owner has no טובת הנאה in the poor-gifts

steps.title: Because the Torah says to leave them
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the תורה uses the language of עזיבה, 'leaving,' for these gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the word 'leave' is written about them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תורה says to 'leave' these gifts, so the owner has no say over who gets them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To 'leave' something means to walk away from it and let anyone eligible take it. If the owner could hand the gifts out to people he chose, he would not really be 'leaving' them. So the word עזיבה removes his טובת הנאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaving or abandoning, from 'תַּעֲזֹב אֹתָם,' 'you shall leave them'
Is written regarding them

steps.whatToRemember: The owner of a field or tree has no טובת הנאה in the poor-gifts, because the תורה says to 'leave' (עזיבה) them for any poor person to take.

phrases.english: 'Leaving' is written regarding them.
phrases.notes: This points to 'תעזב אתם,' 'you shall leave them,' in ויקרא 23:22.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תורה describes these gifts with the word עזיבה, 'leaving,' which takes away the owner's right to choose who receives them.

steps.title: Even a poor owner must leave the gifts
steps.stepSummary: A poor person who owns a field must also leave the poor-gifts, and if he does not, they are taken from him. This is learned from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even a poor person in Israel: we take it out of his hand. As it says: 'Do not gather the gleanings of your harvest; for the poor and the stranger you shall leave them.' This warns a poor person about his own produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the last part of the ברייתא: a poor owner is not exempt from giving the poor-gifts, and the גמרא shows the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think a poor owner could keep the gifts, since he is poor himself. The פסוק puts 'for the poor' right next to the command not to gather, which teaches that even a poor person is warned about his own field. If he keeps the gifts, בית דין takes them from him for other poor people.

keyTerms.meaning: A poor person
They take it out of his hand, meaning בית דין takes the gifts from him
To warn, meaning to teach that a prohibition applies
About his own, meaning his own produce

steps.whatToRemember: The poor-gifts must be given by every owner, even a poor one. A poor owner who keeps them has them taken away for other poor people.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that these gifts are a duty that comes with owning the produce, not just a kindness that only wealthy people must do.

phrases.english: And even a poor person of Israel,
they remove it from his hand,
phrases.notes: If a poor owner keeps the gifts from his own field, בית דין takes them away from him.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'And the gleaning of your harvest you shall not gather;
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:22

phrases.english: for the poor and for the stranger you shall leave them,'
to warn a poor person regarding his own.
phrases.notes: 'For the poor' sits right next to 'you shall not gather,' so the פסוק is warning the poor man about his own field too.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ עָנִי שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מוֹצִיאִין אוֹתוֹ מִיָּדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another rule from the ברייתא: a poor owner is not exempt from the poor-gifts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a poor owner must leave the poor-gifts. If he does not, they are taken from him, as learned from ויקרא 23:22.

steps.title: The owner has a right to choose who gets מעשר עני: why?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that with מעשר עני, which is handed out inside the house, the owner does have טובת הנאה. The גמרא asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The poor man's tithe, which is handed out inside the house, does give the owner the right to choose who gets it. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא, about מעשר עני, and asks why it is different from the field-gifts. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With לקט, שכחה and פאה, the owner has no טובת הנאה because he just leaves them in the field. מעשר עני is the opposite: the owner hands it out himself, so he may pick which poor person gets it. The גמרא wants to know the source for this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The poor man's tithe, separated in the third and sixth years of the שמיטה cycle
That is handed out inside the house, not left in the field
The owner of the produce

phrases.english: And the poor man's tithe, which is handed out inside the house,
the owner has the benefit of choosing who gets it.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and contrasts with step 3, where field-gifts gave no טובת הנאה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for why the owner of מעשר עני has טובת הנאה.

steps.title: Because the תורה calls it 'giving'
steps.stepSummary: The תורה uses the word נתינה, 'giving,' for מעשר עני, so the owner actively gives it and may choose who receives it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'giving' is written about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the פסוק says 'and you shall give' about מעשר עני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors step 4. 'Leaving' (עזיבה) means the owner has no say. 'Giving' (נתינה) means the owner hands it over himself, and a giver may choose his recipient.

keyTerms.meaning: Giving: actively handing something to someone
It is written about it, in the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: עזיבה (leaving) means no טובת הנאה. נתינה (giving) means the owner has טובת הנאה.

phrases.english: 'Giving' is written about it.
phrases.notes: דברים 26:12, 'and you shall give it to the Levite, to the stranger...'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק uses the language of giving for מעשר עני, so the owner chooses the recipient.

steps.title: Even a poor person must separate מעשר עני
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that even a poor Jew who fails to separate מעשר עני from his own produce has it taken from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even a poor Jew: they take it from his possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא: being poor yourself does not exempt you from giving מעשר עני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think a poor person could keep his own מעשר עני, since he is the kind of person it goes to anyway. The ברייתא says no: he must separate it, and if he does not, it is taken from him.

keyTerms.meaning: They take it out of his possession, by force if needed
A poor Jew

phrases.english: And even a poor person among Israel:
they take it out of his hand.
phrases.notes: If he doesn't separate the poor man's tithe from his own crops, it is taken from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ עָנִי שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מוֹצִיאִין אוֹתוֹ מִיָּדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies to מעשר עני the same idea step 5 taught about the field-gifts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A poor person is also obligated to separate מעשר עני, and it is taken from him if he does not.

steps.title: רבי אילעא's source: 'לַגֵּר' and 'לַגֵּר'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא learns from a גזירה שוה of the word 'לַגֵּר' that, just as a poor person must leave לקט from his own field, he must also give מעשר עני from his own produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אילעא said: we learn 'to the stranger' here from 'to the stranger' there. Just as there a poor person is commanded about his own produce, so too here a poor person is commanded about his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the previous rule: the same word appears in both places, so the rule carries over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לַגֵּר' appears for מעשר עני and also for לקט. We already know a poor field-owner must leave לקט (step 5). The matching word passes that rule over to מעשר עני.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns, here by comparing matching words in two פסוקים
To the stranger: the word shared by both פסוקים
Warned, commanded
Just as there… so too here: the pattern of a comparison

phrases.english: As Rabbi Ile'a said:
We learn 'to the stranger' from 'to the stranger' there,
phrases.notes: The same word is used for מעשר עני (דברים 26:12) and for לקט in the פסוק quoted in step 5 (ויקרא 23:22).

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן מוּזְהָר עָנִי עַל שֶׁלּוֹ,
phrases.english: just as there a poor person is warned about his own,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן מוּזְהָר עָנִי עַל שֶׁלּוֹ.
phrases.english: so too here a poor person is warned about his own.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא גָּמַר לַגֵּר לַגֵּר מֵהָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the ruling in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a poor person must separate מעשר עני.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה of 'לַגֵּר' from the מצוה of לקט.

steps.title: Priestly gifts are not taken from one כהן for another, or from one לוי for another
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that other priestly gifts, like the זרוע, לחיים and קבה, are not taken away from a כהן for another כהן, or from a לוי for another לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other priestly gifts, like the foreleg, the jaw and the maw, are not taken away, neither from a כהן for another כהן nor from a לוי for another לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last part of the ברייתא, about the priestly gifts. This line sets up an inference in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the poor-gifts, which are taken even from a poor person, these gifts are not forced out of a כהן or a לוי for someone of the same group. The wording names two pairs, which leaves room for the next step to ask about the pair it does not name: לוי to כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Gifts given to the כהנים
The foreleg, the jaw and the maw (stomach) of an animal, given to a כהן

phrases.english: And the other gifts of the priesthood,
such as the foreleg, the jaw and the maw,
they do not take them away

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מִכֹּהֵן לְכֹהֵן וְלֹא מִלֵּוִי לְלֵוִי.
phrases.english: neither from a priest for a priest, nor from a Levite for a Levite.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁאָר מַתְּנוֹת כְּהוּנָּה כְּגוֹן הַזְּרוֹעַ וְהַלְּחָיַיִם וְהַקֵּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the poor-gifts to the priestly gifts in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Priestly gifts are not taken from a כהן for a כהן or from a לוי for a לוי.

steps.title: Inference: they are taken from a לוי for a כהן, so לוים are 'עם'
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא's wording, the גמרא infers that the gifts are taken from a לוי for a כהן. That would mean לוים count as 'עם,' which settles the earlier doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that from a לוי for a כהן they are taken. So clearly לוים are called 'people.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads between the lines of the ברייתא and uses it to challenge the earlier uncertainty on the daf about whether לוים must give these gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the gifts come 'from the people' (מאת העם). If the gifts are taken from a לוי for a כהן, then a לוי is part of the 'עם' who must give. Since the ברייתא seems to say this clearly, why was there any doubt?

keyTerms.meaning: This implies: introduces an inference from what the text says
Clearly, evidently
They are called 'people,' the group that must give the gifts

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never says 'from a לוי for a כהן.' That is only what the גמרא infers from the cases it leaves out.

phrases.english: This implies: from a Levite for a priest, they do take them,
so clearly they [Levites] are called 'people.'
phrases.notes: דברים 18:3, 'this shall be the priests' due from the people.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מִלֵּוִי לְכֹהֵן מוֹצִיאִין אַלְמָא אִיקְּרוּ עַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording of step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier doubt on the daf about whether לוים must give the priestly gifts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's wording implies the gifts are taken from a לוי for a כהן, which proves לוים are 'עם.'

steps.title: The ברייתא means a gift like the זרוע: מעשר ראשון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'כגון הזרוע' means a gift similar to the זרוע, not the זרוע itself, namely מעשר ראשון. So there is no proof about the זרוע, לחיים and קבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Like the זרוע' means something similar to the זרוע, not the זרוע itself. And what is it? מעשר ראשון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the challenge by rereading the ברייתא's words 'כגון הזרוע.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not talking about the זרוע, לחיים and קבה at all. It is talking about a different gift, מעשר ראשון. So whatever it implies about לוי and כהן does not prove whether לוים are 'עם' for the זרוע, and the earlier doubt stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to the foreleg, but not the foreleg itself
First tithe, given to the לוי
And what is it?

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's ruling is about מעשר ראשון, so it gives no proof about whether לוים count as 'עם' for the זרוע, לחיים and קבה.

phrases.english: 'Like the foreleg,' but not actually the foreleg.
And what is it? First tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by rereading the ברייתא's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the words of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'כגון הזרוע' refers to the actual זרוע, לחיים and קבה, so לוים would be 'עם.'
steps.terutzMaskana: It refers to a gift similar to them, מעשר ראשון, so there is no proof about לוים.

steps.title: But מעשר ראשון belongs to the לוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 12. מעשר ראשון is the לוי's own gift, so why would it be taken from a לוי?
steps.simpleTranslation: But מעשר ראשון belongs to the לוי, doesn't it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own answer that 'כגון הזרוע' means מעשר ראשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא implied that the gift is taken from a לוי and given to a כהן. But the תורה gives מעשר ראשון to the לוי. So it makes no sense to take it away from him.

keyTerms.meaning: First tithe, the tenth of the crop given to the לוי

phrases.english: But first tithe belongs to the Levite!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'כגון הזרוע' refers to מעשר ראשון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מעשר ראשון is the לוי's own gift, so it can't be taken from a לוי for a כהן.

steps.title: The ruling follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who holds that מעשר ראשון may also be given to a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. A ברייתא teaches: תרומה goes to the כהן and מעשר ראשון goes to the לוי; this is רבי עקיבא's view. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: it goes to the כהן too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. In his view, a כהן also has a right to מעשר ראשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי עקיבא, only לוים get מעשר ראשון. According to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, כהנים can get it too. That gives a כהן some claim to it.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion of the crop given to a כהן
To the כהן as well

phrases.english: It follows Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,
as it is taught: Teruma goes to the priest,
first tithe goes to the Levite,
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר: אַף לַכֹּהֵן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says: to the priest as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מעשר ראשון belongs only to the לוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, a כהן also has a share in מעשר ראשון.

steps.title: 'Also to the כהן' doesn't mean 'not to the לוי'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה only added the כהן. He never said the לוי loses it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said 'also to the כהן.' But did he say 'to the כהן and not to the לוי'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Also to the כהן' means both a כהן and a לוי may receive it. If a לוי already has it, he is a proper owner. So there is still no reason to take it from him for a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (grant) that...
Did he say...? (a challenging question)

phrases.aramaic: אֵימַר דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אַף לַכֹּהֵן,
phrases.english: Say that Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya said 'to the priest as well,'
did he say 'to the priest and not to the Levite'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אַף לַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using רבי אלעזר בן עזריה to explain taking the gift from a לוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Adding the כהן as a possible receiver does not remove the לוי's right to keep it.

steps.title: After עזרא penalized the לוים
steps.stepSummary: Yes, it applies after עזרא penalized the לוים. From then on, מעשר ראשון went to the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. It refers to the time after עזרא penalized them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that after עזרא's penalty, the לוים lost their right to מעשר ראשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עזרא fined the לוים, and after that the כהנים received מעשר ראשון. So in that period the gift really belongs to the כהן and could be taken from a לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: A penalty or fine set by the Sages
After

phrases.english: Yes, after Ezra penalized them.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the לוים. עזרא penalized them by stopping their share of מעשר ראשון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a specific time period
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The לוי still has a full right to מעשר ראשון.
steps.terutzMaskana: After עזרא's penalty, the כהן receives מעשר ראשון instead of the לוי.

steps.title: עזרא's penalty did not mean taking it back
steps.stepSummary: עזרא only said not to give the לוים מעשר ראשון. He never said to take it away from them once they have it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, עזרא penalized them so that we don't give it to them. But did he say we take it away from them?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back again, this time on the עזרא answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not giving something and taking it back are two different things. The penalty only stopped new giving. Our ברייתא, though, talks about taking the gift out of the person's hands.

keyTerms.meaning: We give
To take from them

phrases.english: Say that Ezra penalized them,
so that we do not give to them;
but did he say to take it from them?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using עזרא's penalty to explain why the gift is taken from a לוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The penalty only stopped giving to the לוים. It did not allow taking back what they already hold.

steps.title: The gift is ראשית הגז
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the מעשר ראשון answer. 'Like the זרוע' now means ראשית הגז.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means something like the זרוע but not the זרוע. And what is it? ראשית הגז.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer: the gift that is taken from a לוי for a כהן is ראשית הגז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ראשית הגז is a gift from a regular animal, like the זרוע, which is why it is 'like the זרוע.' But its פסוק (דברים 18:4) does not say 'from the people,' so even a לוי must give it, and it can be taken from him for a כהן. So the ברייתא still proves nothing about whether a לוי must give the זרוע, לחיים and קבה.

keyTerms.meaning: The first shearing of wool, given to a כהן
And what is it?

steps.whatToRemember: The final reading of 'כגון הזרוע' is ראשית הגז, not the זרוע itself. So this ברייתא does not settle רב's doubt about whether לוים count as 'עם'. The גמרא keeps testing that doubt in steps 19–30.

phrases.english: Rather, it means like the foreleg, but not the foreleg itself,
and what is it? The first shearing.
phrases.notes: דברים 18:4

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the מעשר ראשון answer from Step 12, which failed in Step 17.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Like the זרוע' means ראשית הגז, which may be taken from a לוי for a כהן.

steps.title: A rule: holy gifts are taken, non-holy gifts are not
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא says holy gifts are taken away, but the זרוע, לחיים and קבה are not. This seems to prove that לוים are exempt from those gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: This is the rule. Anything that is holy, like תרומה, תרומת מעשר and חלה, is taken out of their hands. Anything that is not holy, like the זרוע, לחיים and קבה, is not taken out of their hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to try to settle רב's doubt about whether לוים must give the זרוע, לחיים and קבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא splits the gifts in two. Holy gifts, which a non-כהן may not eat, are taken from a לוי. Non-holy gifts like the זרוע, לחיים and קבה are not taken. That seems to show that לוים are not counted as 'עם' and don't have to give these gifts.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
Holy, not allowed to be eaten by a non-כהן
The tenth that the לוי gives from his מעשר to the כהן
The portion of dough given to a כהן
They take them out of their hands

steps.confusionAlert: 'Their hands' here means the לוים. The question is only whether the gift is taken from a לוי for a כהן.

phrases.english: Come and hear: This is the rule:
anything that is holy,
such as teruma, teruma of the tithe, and challa,
is taken out of their hands,
and anything that is not holy,
such as the foreleg, the jaw, and the maw,
is not taken out of their hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was pushed off in Step 18, the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: רב's doubt about whether לוים count as 'עם' and must give the זרוע, לחיים and קבה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the rule that holy gifts are taken from them but the זרוע, לחיים and קבה are not

steps.title: The ברייתא means something like the זרוע, namely מעשר ראשון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא is talking about a gift that is like the זרוע but is not the זרוע itself. That gift is מעשר ראשון after עזרא's penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means something like the זרוע, but not the זרוע itself. What is it? מעשר ראשון, in the time after עזרא penalized the לוים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from the last ברייתא. It says the ברייתא is not talking about the real זרוע, לחיים and קבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 seemed to prove that לוים do not have to give the זרוע, לחיים and קבה. The גמרא now says the ברייתא only meant a gift that works like them: מעשר ראשון after עזרא gave it to the כהנים. If a לוי already has it, nobody takes it from him, so the ברייתא says nothing about the real מתנות.

keyTerms.meaning: First tithe, which normally goes to the לוי
עזרא's penalty on the לוים, so that מעשר ראשון was given to כהנים
Like, similar to

steps.confusionAlert: Step 18 seemed to drop the מעשר ראשון answer. Here the גמרא uses it again to read this new ברייתא, so 'like the זרוע' now refers to מעשר ראשון after עזרא.

phrases.english: Something like the foreleg, but not the foreleg itself,
phrases.notes: He means a gift that works like the זרוע, לחיים and קבה but is a different gift.

phrases.english: and what is it? First tithe,
and in the time after Ezra penalized them.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the לוים, as in step 16.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 19
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Removes the ברייתא as evidence about the real זרוע, לחיים and קבה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'זרוע' meant the actual מתנות. It can mean a similar gift, מעשר ראשון after עזרא.

steps.title: A new ברייתא: slaughtering for a כהן or a גוי is exempt
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that slaughtering for a כהן or a גוי is exempt from the מתנות. That seems to mean that slaughtering for a לוי or a ישראל is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: one who slaughters for a כהן or for a גוי is exempt from the gifts. That implies that one who slaughters for a לוי or for a ישראל is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא as a proof. It tries to infer that a לוי must give the מתנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא names only the כהן and the גוי as exempt. So it seems that everyone else, including a לוי, must give. That would show that לוים are part of the 'people,' and רב should not have been unsure.

keyTerms.meaning: The gifts from a slaughtered animal: the זרוע, לחיים and קבה, given to a כהן
Exempt
Obligated

phrases.english: Come and hear: one who slaughters for a priest or for a gentile
phrases.notes: He means the animal belongs to the כהן or the גוי, and someone else does the slaughtering.

phrases.english: is exempt from the gifts,
which implies that for a Levite or for an Israelite, he is obligated?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the last proof was pushed away, a new proof is brought
steps.raayaObject: That a לוי must give the מתנות, so לוים count as part of the 'people'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that lists only a כהן and a גוי as exempt

steps.title: Read the ברייתא as implying only a ישראל is obligated
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference. It says we should not infer that a לוי is obligated, only that a ישראל is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't say it implies that a לוי or a ישראל is obligated. Say instead that only a ישראל is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to escape the proof by changing what we infer from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof rested on the idea that 'not a כהן or a גוי' means 'a לוי or a ישראל.' The גמרא suggests the inference only covers a ישראל. That leaves the status of a לוי open.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't say this; say that instead. The גמרא's way of rereading an inference.

phrases.aramaic: לָא תֵּימָא הָא לְלֵוִי וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵל חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: Do not say: for a Levite or an Israelite, he is obligated,
rather, say: for an Israelite, he is obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא הָא לְלֵוִי וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵל חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 21
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the part of the inference about the לוי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed the ברייתא's implication had to include the לוי

steps.title: If a לוי is exempt, the ברייתא should have said so
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the rereading. If a לוי were exempt, the ברייתא should have written 'a לוי and a גוי,' and we would know about a כהן on our own.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then for a לוי, what? Exempt? If so, it should teach: one who slaughters for a לוי or for a גוי is exempt from the gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rereading from step 22 by asking how the ברייתא is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a לוי were exempt, then a כהן would surely be exempt, since he is the one who receives the gifts. So the ברייתא should have named the לוי, because that teaches more. Naming the כהן suggests that the לוי is not exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let it teach; it should have said

phrases.english: But for a Levite, what? Exempt?
If so, let it teach:
"One who slaughters for a Levite or for a gentile is exempt from the gifts."
phrases.notes: Then a כהן would be exempt all the more, so he would not need to be mentioned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל לְלֵוִי מַאי פָּטוּר? אִי הָכִי, לִיתְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: The rereading that leaves the לוי possibly exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the לוי were exempt, the ברייתא should have named him, since that teaches the most

steps.title: An explicit ברייתא refutes רב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא openly says that slaughtering for a לוי or a ישראל is obligated. This is a full refutation of רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And besides, it was taught: one who slaughters for a כהן or for a גוי is exempt from the gifts; for a לוי or a ישראל, he is obligated. This refutes רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger challenge. A ברייתא states outright that a לוי must give the מתנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we do not need any inference, because this ברייתא names the לוי as obligated. That clearly means לוים count as part of the 'people.' So the גמרא declares a תיובתא against רב's uncertainty.

keyTerms.meaning: And besides; an added challenge
A full refutation

phrases.english: And furthermore, isn't it taught:

phrases.aramaic: הַשּׁוֹחֵט לַכֹּהֵן וְלַגּוֹי – פָּטוּר מִן הַמַּתָּנוֹת,
phrases.english: One who slaughters for a priest or for a gentile is exempt from the gifts,
for a Levite or for an Israelite, he is obligated!
This is a refutation of Rav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, explicit challenge after step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's uncertainty about whether לוים are part of the 'people'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא openly rules that a לוי is obligated in the מתנות

steps.title: רב: this is a מחלוקת between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers for רב that whether לוים count as the 'people' is a מחלוקת of תנאים. It starts bringing a ברייתא on the יום כיפור atonement to show it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב can say to you: it is a dispute between תנאים. As it was taught: 'And he shall atone for the holy sanctuary' means the innermost part, the קודש הקדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב: other תנאים disagree with this ברייתא, so it does not refute him. The גמרא is setting up a longer ברייתא that will show this disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב does not deny the ברייתא. He says it reflects only one תנא's view, and another תנא holds that לוים are not called the 'people.' The ברייתא begins explaining the פסוק of יום כיפור one phrase at a time, and the key part about the 'people' comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a disagreement between תנאים
And he shall atone; said about the כהן גדול on יום כיפור
The innermost sanctum, the קודש הקדשים

steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רב from the refutation by showing that his doubt matches a real disagreement between תנאים.

phrases.english: Rav could say to you: it is a dispute between tanna'im,
as it is taught: "And he shall make atonement for the holy sanctuary":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:33

phrases.english: this is the innermost sanctum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the תיובתא in step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ruling is a מחלוקת between תנאים, so רב can follow the other side
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא proves that all agree a לוי is obligated, so רב is refuted
steps.terutzMaskana: Only one תנא holds this. Another תנא may hold that לוים are not part of the 'people.'

steps.title: The first ברייתא reads each phrase of the יום כיפור פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes phrase by phrase through the פסוק and ends by using the last 'יכפר' to include the לוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Tent of Meeting' means the היכל. 'Altar' means what it says. 'He shall atone' means the courtyards. 'Priests' means what it says. 'People of the assembly' means ישראל. 'He shall atone' means the לוים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the ברייתא it started quoting in the previous step. Each phrase of the פסוק is tied to a place or a group that the יום כיפור offerings atone for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key line is the last one. This ברייתא already has ישראל covered by 'עם הקהל', yet it still needs an extra 'יכפר' to bring in the לוים. That suggests this תנא holds that לוים are NOT included in the word 'עם'.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary building in the בית המקדש
As it sounds; its plain meaning
The courtyards of the בית המקדש
The people of the assembly
He shall atone; the extra word used here to include another group

phrases.english: 'Tent of Meeting': this is the Sanctuary.
phrases.notes: This is ויקרא 16:33, the פסוק about what the יום כיפור offerings atone for.

phrases.english: 'Altar': as it sounds.
'He shall atone': these are the courtyards.
'Priests': as it sounds.
'People of the assembly': these are the Israelites.
'He shall atone': these are the Levites.
phrases.notes: Watch this line. The לוים needed their own word, so they were not counted inside 'עם'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that רב's answer began quoting in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That one תנא holds לוים are not part of 'עם'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's use of a separate 'יכפר' to include the לוים.

steps.title: A second ברייתא uses the same word for slaves
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא reads 'יכפר' as including slaves, not לוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: 'He shall atone': these are slaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that uses the very same word 'יכפר' for a different group: slaves. This sets up the comparison in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this תנא uses 'יכפר' for slaves, he has no extra word left for the לוים. So he must hold that the לוים are already included somewhere else, most likely in 'עם הקהל'.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaves; here, non-Jewish slaves owned by Jews, who keep some מצוות
Atonement
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: And another ברייתא teaches:
'He shall atone': these are slaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a contrasting ברייתא to set against step 26.
steps.raayaObject: That a second תנא holds לוים are part of 'עם'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: This ברייתא uses 'יכפר' for slaves, leaving no extra word for the לוים.

steps.title: The two ברייתות argue about whether לוים are called 'עם'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the two ברייתות disagree on whether לוים count as 'עם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this what they argue about? One Sage holds the לוים are called 'עם', and the other Sage holds they are not called 'עם'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts the two ברייתות side by side and names their disagreement. This proves רב's point from step 25: it is a מחלוקת of תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא about slaves holds that לוים ARE called 'עם', so 'יכפר' is free to include slaves. The ברייתא about לוים holds they are NOT called 'עם', so it needs 'יכפר' just for them. Now רב is no longer refuted by one ברייתא, because other תנאים disagree with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? (offering a likely explanation)
They argue
One Sage holds
They are called 'people'

steps.whatToRemember: The question of whether לוים are 'עם' is a real מחלוקת between תנאים, so רב's view has support.

phrases.english: Is it not that they disagree about this:
that one Sage holds they are called 'people',
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא about slaves: the לוים are already inside 'עם הקהל'.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds they are not called 'people'.
phrases.notes: This is the first ברייתא, which needed a separate 'יכפר' for the לוים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from comparing steps 26 and 27.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: תנאים argue whether לוים are called 'עם', which backs up רב's answer in step 25.

steps.title: Why doesn't רב just choose a side?
steps.stepSummary: If this is a מחלוקת of תנאים, רב should simply rule like one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב: if he holds like this תנא, let him say so; and if he holds like that תנא, let him say so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב. If there are two clear opinions, why does רב not just pick one and give a clear ruling?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually an אמורא who knows about a מחלוקת of תנאים sides with one of them. Since רב seems to leave the matter open, the גמרא asks why he does not decide.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this opinion)
A Sage of the משנה or ברייתא period
Let him say

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב, אִי סְבִירָא לֵיהּ כְּהַאי תַּנָּא – לֵימָא,
phrases.english: And רב: if he holds like this תנא, let him say so,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סְבִירָא לֵיהּ כְּהַאי תַּנָּא – לֵימָא!
phrases.english: and if he holds like that תנא, let him say so!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב, אִי סְבִירָא לֵיהּ כְּהַאי תַּנָּא – לֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רב's position now that the מחלוקת is established.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's open stance on the status of לוים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If two clear opinions exist, an אמורא should side with one of them instead of staying undecided.

steps.title: רב is unsure which תנא is right
steps.stepSummary: רב does not choose because he is truly in doubt between the two תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is unsure whether the הלכה follows this תנא or that תנא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב has a real doubt. He does not know which תנא the הלכה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's view is not a third opinion. It is a ספק about which of the two opinions is correct. So the status of a לוי for the מתנות stays uncertain.

keyTerms.meaning: He is in doubt
A doubt; an unresolved question

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying לוים are definitely exempt or definitely obligated. He is saying the matter is in doubt.

phrases.english: He is uncertain

phrases.aramaic: אִי כְּהַאי תַּנָּא אִי כְּהַאי תַּנָּא.
phrases.english: whether it is like this תנא or like that תנא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies that רב's position is a doubt, not a firm ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב should have picked one תנא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב is truly unsure which תנא is correct, so he leaves it as a ספק.

steps.title: מרימר rules like רב and like רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: מרימר teaches that the הלכה follows רב and also follows רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר taught: the הלכה follows רב, and the הלכה follows רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion with a final ruling. מרימר says we follow רב on the לוים and רב חסדא on his earlier ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רב means the status of a לוי stays in doubt, so a לוי cannot be forced to give the מתנות to a כהן. Following רב חסדא refers to his earlier ruling that someone who damages or eats the מתנות is exempt from paying.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught publicly
The הלכה follows him
The gifts given to a כהן: foreleg, jaw, and stomach

steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכה: we follow רב (the לוי's status is in doubt) and רב חסדא (one who damages or eats the מתנות does not pay).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line for whether a לוי must give the מתנות from his own animals.

phrases.english: מרימר taught: the הלכה follows רב,
phrases.notes: This means a לוי's status stays in doubt, so we can't force him to give the gifts.

phrases.english: and the הלכה follows רב חסדא.
phrases.notes: This points back to רב חסדא's earlier ruling: one who damages or eats the gifts does not pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final הלכה after רב's position has been explained.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רב, so a לוי's obligation is in doubt, and follows רב חסדא, so one who damages or eats the מתנות is exempt.

steps.title: עולא gave the gifts to a female from a כהן family
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that עולא's practice was to give the gifts of כהונה to a כהנת.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא used to give the gifts to a כהנת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by telling us what עולא used to do: he gave the gifts of כהונה to a כהנת. This sets up רבא's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא's practice assumes that when the תורה gives gifts to 'the כהן', it also includes a female from a כהן family. This assumption is the target of the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The gifts of כהונה that this perek is about
A female from a כהן family, such as the daughter of a כהן

phrases.english: Ulla would give
the gifts to a female priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after מרימר's ruling closed the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, עולא gave the gifts of כהונה to a כהנת.

steps.title: רבא challenges עולא from the law of a כהנת's מנחה
steps.stepSummary: רבא cites a ברייתא: a כהנת's מנחה is eaten, but a כהן's מנחה is not. So the word 'כהן' cannot include a כהנת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged עולא: A כהנת's מנחה is eaten, but a כהן's מנחה is not eaten. If you say 'כהן' includes even a כהנת, the פסוק says: 'Every מנחה of a כהן shall be completely burned; it shall not be eaten'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks עולא's practice using a ברייתא about מנחות. He argues that if 'כהן' included a כהנת, her מנחה could not be eaten either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a כהן's מנחה must be completely burned. Yet the ברייתא says a כהנת's מנחה is eaten, so in that פסוק the word 'כהן' clearly does not include her. In the same way, the gifts that the תורה gives to 'the כהן' should not go to a כהנת.

keyTerms.meaning: A flour offering brought on the מזבח
Is eaten (the leftover part of the מנחה is eaten by כהנים)
Completely burned on the מזבח, with nothing eaten
And if you say (introduces the conclusion the questioner is pushing back on)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up כֹּהֶנֶת (a female from a כהן family) with כֹּהֵן (a male כהן). The whole challenge depends on the law for each one being different.

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection to Ulla:
the meal offering of a female priest is eaten,
the meal offering of a priest is not eaten.
And if you say that 'priest' means even a female priest,
but isn't it written: 'And every meal offering of a priest
shall be completely burned; it shall not be eaten'!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:16

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practice reported in step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's practice of giving the gifts of כהונה to a כהנת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the פסוק about a מנחה, 'כהן' does not include a כהנת, because her מנחה is eaten. So in the gifts, 'כהן' should not include her either.

steps.title: עולא begins his reply
steps.stepSummary: עולא starts to answer רבא, respectfully calling him 'רבי'. The answer itself continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said to him: My teacher,
steps.whatsHappening: This line only opens עולא's answer to רבא's challenge. The actual answer comes in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far, עולא has only begun to speak by respectfully addressing רבא. What he will actually say comes next. The learner should expect him to explain why the מנחה law does not decide the question of the gifts.

keyTerms.meaning: My teacher (a respectful way of addressing someone)

phrases.english: He said to him: My teacher,
phrases.notes: עולא is speaking to רבא here, and the rest of his answer continues on the next part of the daf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the defense against רבא's challenge in step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Not yet stated; the answer continues on the next part of the daf.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's challenge seems to show that a כהנת should not receive the gifts.
